correctness.rationale: For any linear isomorphism \(T\) to a Euclidean space, equivalence of \(N\) with \(|x|_T=\|Tx\|_2\) gives \(C_{\mathrm{Pt}}(X)\le(\|T\|\|T^{-1}\|)^2\), hence \(C_{\mathrm{Pt}}(X)\le d_{\mathrm{BM}}(X,\ell_2^2)^2\). The source exact Ptolemy values therefore give lower bounds \(\sqrt2\lambda\) and \(\lambda\), while the elementary inequalities \(\|x\|_1\le\sqrt2\|x\|_2\) and \(\|x\|_\infty\le\|x\|_2\) give identical upper bounds. Endpoint cases were checked and no numerical or finite-exhaustion step is used.

value.rationale: The Banach--Mazur distance is an affine invariant, so a coordinate norm comparison alone does not normally certify optimality against all linear changes of variables. Here two natural literature-defined disk/diamond and disk/square max-norm families admit exact global distances because the Ptolemy constants saturate a universal distortion lower bound. This supplies exact affine geometry for continuous parameter families and a reusable certificate pattern rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
